items.q: What did BridgeMind actually compare in this four-model test?
items.a: A **same-prompt bake-off** of **Kimi K3**, **Fable 5**, **GPT 5.6**, and **Grok 4.5** — each in its native harness (Kimi Code, Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build) across three BridgeSpace workspaces: Next.js therapy frontend, full-stack AI therapist, and an Angry Birds–style game.
Output quality, plan usage, and especially **inference speed** — because vibe coding often needs fast iteration more than max intelligence.

items.q: How did the four models compare on tokens per second and latency?
items.a: Open Router snapshot: Grok **55 tok/s** / **1.45s** TTFT; Fable ~**43**; GPT 5.6 ~**40**; Kimi **17 tok/s** / ~**14s** latency — down from ~27 tok/s at launch. After 25+ minutes Grok had finished all tasks while Kimi was still early on todos.

items.q: Why did Kimi get demoted despite strong design?
items.a: Full-stack Kimi took ~**90 minutes**, and at 17 tok/s + 14s latency it was framed as **almost unusable** for daily workflow — **serving capacity** (Moonshot pausing new subs, withholding open weights) became the product constraint.

items.q: Who won frontend UI, game, and full-stack?
items.a: Frontend: **Kimi best** (green therapy aesthetic, chart polish) → Fable → GPT → Grok. Game: **Fable** slight edge over GPT; Grok **non-functional**. Full-stack: **Fable oneshot** with working AI therapist; GPT Hermes crash loop; Grok chat broken; Kimi realtime handshake fails.

items.q: What was BridgeMind's personal workflow ranking?
items.a: **Fable 5 → GPT 5.6 → Grok 4.5 → Kimi K3**. Route Fable for hard polish/oneshots, Grok for cheap fast iteration (~**$0.31**/task), GPT as #2 — and avoid slow Kimi despite UI genius.

items.q: How does Cloud plan access change the routing story?
items.a: Fable stays on **Cloud Max**; **Cloud Pro** loses Fable (tweet ~Jul 17) — so Pro users should switch toward Codex. Grok remains affordable **iterate fuel**.

items.q: Which harness had the worst hallucination callout?
items.a: Codex/GPT at **89%** hallucination vs Fable **54** / Grok **53** / Kimi **~51** — cited as a driver of catastrophic agent failures like deleting prod codebases.
